findings.explanation: The Webex Meeting Qualities API returns per-media-session arrays of packetLoss, latency, jitter, frameRate, mediaBitRate and resolutionHeight for audioIn/audioOut/videoIn/videoOut/shareIn/shareOut. It has no MOS value, so the MOS threshold and its 'Poor Audio MOS' bucket cannot be built from this feed.
findings.quote: Set alert thresholds: MOS < 3.5, packet loss > 5%, jitter > 30 ms, latency > 300 ms.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the MOS threshold, or state that MOS has to be estimated from latency/jitter/loss (for example an E-model approximation). Express thresholds against the real metrics: audioIn/audioOut packetLoss %, latency ms and jitter ms per sampling interval.

findings.explanation: Webex documents no 10-minute minimum polling interval. The 10 minutes is the delay before quality data becomes available after a meeting starts, and the stated limit is one call every 5 minutes per meeting instance ID. The text also omits that the API is queried per meetingId, which means listing meetings first.
findings.quote: Configure a modular input to poll the Webex Meeting Qualities API every 10 minutes (the minimum interval allowed).
findings.suggested_fix: Say that quality data appears about 10 minutes after a meeting starts and stays retrievable for 7 days; the API is rate-limited to one call per meeting instance every 5 minutes. Use the Cisco Webex Add-on's 'Webex Meeting Qualities' input, which handles meeting enumeration and checkpointing.

findings.explanation: The Cisco Webex Add-on for Splunk ships a dedicated 'Webex Meeting Qualities' input that writes `cisco:webex:meeting:qualities`. It is a REST modular input run on a heavy forwarder or search head; the Universal Forwarder (617) cannot run it and plays no part. The dataSources field repeats the same UF claim.
findings.quote: `ta_cisco_webex_add_on_for_splunk` (GitHub), Webex Meeting Qualities API (Pro Pack required) — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
findings.suggested_fix: App: Cisco Webex Add-on for Splunk (`ta_cisco_webex_add_on_for_splunk`), 'Webex Meeting Qualities' input (sourcetype `cisco:webex:meeting:qualities`, scope analytics:read_all), run on a heavy forwarder or Splunk Cloud IDM. Remove the Universal Forwarder reference from app and dataSources.

findings.explanation: The description and controlTest name scalar fields (audioMOS, videoPacketLoss, audioJitter, audioLatency, participantEmail, meetingId) and the sourcetype `webex:meeting_quality`. None of these exist in the API response, which uses webexUserEmail, meetingInstanceId and nested arrays, or in the add-on's `cisco:webex:meeting:qualities` sourcetype. Readers who follow the prose will look for fields that do not exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the detection with the real structure: per participant (webexUserEmail) per meeting (meetingInstanceId), expand audioIn{}/videoIn{} arrays and flag sampling intervals where packetLoss, latency or jitter exceed the thresholds.

findings.explanation: The Meeting Qualities API covers Webex Meetings media sessions only. Webex Calling quality comes from other sources such as Detailed Call History or calling quality reports.
findings.quote: Supports SLA reporting and vendor accountability for Webex Calling and Meetings.
findings.suggested_fix: Limit the claim to Webex Meetings; point to the Webex Calling UCs (for example UC-11.3.15) for calling quality.

findings.explanation: The Cisco Security support index has nothing to do with Webex meeting quality. The Webex Meeting Qualities API reference and the add-on README are the sources a reader needs.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: Uses the invented sourcetype `webex:meeting_quality` and scalar fields audioMOS, videoPacketLoss, audioJitter, audioLatency, participantEmail and meetingId. The add-on writes `cisco:webex:meeting:qualities`, and the API returns webexUserEmail, meetingInstanceId and per-interval arrays under audioIn{}/videoIn{} (no MOS). The search will return nothing. Rewrite with spath/mvexpand over audioIn{}.packetLoss{}, latency{} and jitter{}. Evidence: https://developer.webex.com/docs/api/v1/meeting-qualities/get-meeting-qualities

summary: The Webex licensing and scope facts are right (Pro Pack, analytics:read_all, 10-minute delay, 7-day window), but the UC relies on a MOS metric the Meeting Qualities API does not return. It also invents scalar field names and a sourcetype, and describes the official add-on's built-in input as a generic UF modular input.
